description: Write to a temp file and rename it into place instead of writing the destination directly, so a crash mid-write never leaves a half-written config file
prompts: scripts/write_config.sh writes its input DIRECTLY to the destination file - if the process is killed partway through (or the disk fills up), readers can observe a half-written, corrupt file, and there is no way to distinguish 'old content' from 'garbage mid-write'. Fix it to write atomically: write the content to a temp file in the SAME directory as the destination (same filesystem, so the final rename is atomic - a temp file elsewhere could make `mv` fall back to a non-atomic copy across filesystems), then `mv` that temp file onto the destination path. Also clean up the temp file with a trap if the script exits before the rename (e.g. content generation fails) so it doesn't leak stray temp files. The destination's final content for a successful run must be byte-identical to before.

setup_files.scripts/write_config.sh:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
# Writes directly to the destination - not atomic, a mid-write crash
# leaves a corrupt partial file.
DEST=$1
cat > "$DEST"

reference_solution.scripts/write_config.sh:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

DEST=$1
DEST_DIR=$(dirname "$DEST")
TMP=$(mktemp "$DEST_DIR/.write_config.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f "$TMP"' EXIT

cat > "$TMP"
mv "$TMP" "$DEST"
trap - EXIT

files.scripts/write_config.sh:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

DEST=$1
DEST_DIR=$(dirname "$DEST")
TMP=$(mktemp "$DEST_DIR/.write_config.XXXXXX")

cat > "$TMP"
cp "$TMP" "$DEST"
mv "$TMP" "$TMP.bak"

test_setup_files.check_write_config.py:
"""Behavioral checks for scripts/write_config.sh, run with the real bash."""
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

SCRIPT = "scripts/write_config.sh"


def run(dest, stdin_text, timeout=10):
    return subprocess.run(
        ["bash", SCRIPT, dest],
        input=stdin_text, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout,
    )


workdir = Path("cfg_check_tmp")
workdir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
dest = workdir / "app.conf"

# 1. A normal successful write must produce the exact content, no leftovers.
proc = run(str(dest), "key=value\n")
assert proc.returncode == 0, f"write failed: {proc.stdout}{proc.stderr}"
assert dest.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "key=value\n", "content mismatch after write"

leftovers = [p for p in workdir.iterdir() if p.name != "app.conf"]
assert not leftovers, f"temp files leaked into the destination directory: {leftovers}"

# 2. Overwriting must never leave the OLD content readable mid-write, nor
#    leave a temp artifact behind - check the write goes through mv (rename),
#    which is what the expected_files gate already enforces structurally;
#    here we confirm a second write still cleanly replaces content.
proc = run(str(dest), "key=updated\n")
assert proc.returncode == 0
assert dest.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "key=updated\n"
leftovers = [p for p in workdir.iterdir() if p.name != "app.conf"]
assert not leftovers, f"temp files leaked on overwrite: {leftovers}"

print("PASS write_config.sh atomicity checks")
